# m=500 campaign tables (full-span evaluation, monitoring off, tuning on the first 30%)

Per arm: recall / precision / specificity (reported set) / speedup vs bruteforce (same job). CT-lsh = CorrTrack lsh_sign_dot (own hyperopt), CT-ham = CorrTrack lsh_hamming_exact + dot gate (own hyperopt); competitors tuned by the CSZ protocol (StatStream, ParCorr, CSZ, CorrJoin), BRAID/ThinBRAID at paper defaults. N/A = arm not available under the table's protocol. `*` = cell pending the memory-mode rerun (see log 2026-09-22 (b)). Tuning walls per cell in the last column: lsh hyperopt / hamming hyperopt / CSZ tuning (s).

## Table 1. Speedup over brute force at equal tuned recall, by correlation threshold, capability class and data space

Median over the six real datasets of each method's wall-clock speedup over the brute-force baseline measured in the same job, with the median achieved recall in brackets. Rows are grouped by capability class (S: synchronous and positive correlation only; L: lagged, positive; N: lagged, both signs), by data space (raw levels, cooperative; first differences, uncooperative) and by correlation threshold T. The density column gives the median fraction of the tested pair-windows that brute force confirms correlated at that threshold, which decreases by four orders of magnitude across the rows and is what separates the regimes. Within a row every method solves the same problem on the same data with its own tuned parameters, so the columns are directly comparable; across rows only the ordering is, since the underlying work changes with T. An empty cell means the method does not support that class.

`*` the method does not reach the tuned recall target of 0.95 in that cell, so its speedup is not read at equal recall: it buys speed with misses. Across the campaign this affects StatStream in 141 of 141 cells (median recall 0.025; its own tuning reports no feasible setting in 140 of 142 cells), ThinBRAID in 133 of 143 (median 0.815), CSZ in 25 of 95, ParCorr in 15 of 95, and CorrTrack itself in 11 of 143 cells for the lsh backend and 5 of 143 for the hamming backend (lowest 0.76 and 0.73, in the densest raw cells).

`†` parameters are the method's published defaults, not selected by the tuning protocol, which does not apply to BRAID and ThinBRAID.

`‡` the capability the class requires is not the authors' but ours, so the result characterises our extension rather than the published method: ParCorr and CSZ are synchronous by construction and reach class L through a lag extension of ours, and FilCorr rejects negative correlation until we enable it, which is how it enters class N. The runs record this per arm (supports_neg_corr = enabled_by_us for FilCorr).

`¶` the capability is specified in the paper but never evaluated there, so the result is our evaluation of their design: StatStream defines lag handling without measuring it, and BRAID, ThinBRAID and StatStream define negative correlation without measuring it (supports_neg_corr = specified).

`§` the method emits its own approximate decision instead of a set that has passed exact validation, so unlike every other arm its precision and specificity can fall below 1. ThinBRAID exercises that freedom (up to 190 false positives per true one) and StatStream reports too few pair-windows to be read as a decision at all, while BRAID's lag interpolation happens to be exact on these lag grids and it reports precisely the brute-force set. Recall, precision and specificity in these tables are exact for every arm: the reported set is intersected with the brute-force truth. The one bounded quantity is the candidate-stage specificity recorded in the result files and not shown here, since the true positives among an approximate arm's candidates are unknown.

Two further caveats apply to every competitor column and are stated once rather than per cell. All competitor arms are our reimplementations inside this codebase, while CorrTrack carries months of Cython optimisation, so wall-clock ratios between them mix algorithm and implementation; the candidate counters in the per-cell tables are the implementation-independent comparison. StatStream's zero recall on every differenced cell is under investigation as a defect of our port rather than a property of the published method.

**Legend and configuration.**

| item | value |
|---|---|
| Datasets (m x T) | streamflow 500 x 2768, sp500 444 x 2768, wikipedia 500 x 2768, smartmeter 500 x 27649, global_weather 500 x 2768, acwi_capweighted 500 x 2768; deterministic-prefix cuts of build_m500_cuts.py, one median per cell over the six |
| Window protocol | W = 30, step = 3, lags 0 (class S) or 15 (classes L and N), i.e. L = 6 lagged windows; smartmeter W = 48, step = 8, lags 0 or 16 |
| Correlation thresholds | 0.70, 0.80, 0.90, 0.95 (Pearson, exact validation for every arm) |
| Data spaces | raw levels (cooperative) and first differences (uncooperative); ground truth, tuning and every arm run in the cell's own space |
| Capability classes | S: n_lags = 0, positive correlation; L: lagged, positive; N: lagged, positive and negative. Each class is tuned and run separately, so no method is compared with parameters tuned for a different problem |
| Tuning span / evaluation span | parameters are selected on the first 30% of each stream (TRAIN_RATIO = 0.3); every method is then evaluated on the whole stream |
| CorrTrack tuning | its own proxy-anchor hyperopt, target recall 0.95. CT-lsh: lsh_sign_dot grid of 80 settings (n_vectors 32/64 x gamma offset 0/0.05/0.10/0.20 x target occupancy 2/3/5/8/12 x hamming filter fraction none/0.40); CT-ham: lsh_hamming_exact + dot gate, 8 settings (n_vectors x gamma offset) |
| Competitor tuning | Cole, Shasha and Zhao's protocol (KDD 2005, section 5.4): strength-2 covering array, coordinate refinement, then a block bootstrap; a setting is feasible when its bootstrap recall lower bound reaches 0.95 and its precision reaches 0.02, and the feasible setting with the fewest candidates is chosen. Applied to ParCorr, CSZ, StatStream and CorrJoin; the calibration span is capped at 64 windows of 300 series |
| Untuned arms | BRAID and ThinBRAID run at their published defaults (b = 16, gamma = 0.4, thinning d0 = 400), since the CSZ protocol does not apply to them; TSUBASA, STOMP and full-band FilCorr are exact and have no recall knob |
| Availability rules | ParCorr, CSZ and CorrJoin provide no negative correlation, so they are absent from class N; TSUBASA and CorrJoin are synchronous by construction, so they are absent from classes L and N. ParCorr and CSZ appear in class L through a lag extension of ours, not of their authors |
| Speedup | wall clock of the brute-force arm divided by the wall clock of the method, both measured in the same job on the same node, monitoring disabled for every arm |
| Recall | fraction of the brute-force correlated pair-windows the method reports, at its tuned setting on the evaluation span. Precision and specificity are in the per-cell tables; every exact-validation arm reaches precision 1.0 by construction |
| Measurement | each arm runs in its own forked process with its own CPU, memory and energy accounting; correlated sets are transferred in memory, so no arm pays for disk in its measured time |
| Hardware and software | Grid'5000 Sophia, cluster mercantour3, one whole node per comparison (2 x Intel Xeon Silver 4114, 20 cores, 192 GB), sequential single-threaded execution with BLAS threads pinned to 1; Python 3.12.14, numpy 1.26.4, one frozen build for the whole campaign |
| Cells | 143 of 144 (six datasets x four thresholds x two spaces x three classes, minus the synchronous smartmeter cell at T = 0.95 on differences, whose calibration span contains no correlated pair and which therefore cannot be tuned) |
